playbook:
When I'm asked to declare, I usually declare my true private yield unless a clear tactical reason to under-declare appears.  
When my private yield is very low (1–2), I declare it honestly and deposit the full declared amount to signal cooperation.  
When my private yield is moderate (3–7), I declare it honestly and plan to deposit roughly half to two-thirds of the declared amount (round to an integer) to balance group benefit and personal score.  
When my private yield is high (8–10), consider under-declaring by a few units only if I want to limit the amount I am expected to deposit and the opponent has been free‑riding; otherwise declare honestly to keep flexibility.  
When under-declaring, never plan to deposit more than the declared amount (audit checks this), and make the under-declaration small enough that it doesn’t invite reciprocal non-cooperation.  

When I'm asked to deposit, use past opponent behavior to set the contribution:  
- If the opponent has been contributing near zero repeatedly, reduce my deposit (keep more private) and deposit a low to moderate amount (0 to about one-third of declared) to avoid being exploited.  
- If the opponent has been contributing at least moderate amounts consistently, deposit half to two-thirds of my declared harvest to build mutual gains.  
- If it's the final round and the opponent has been exploiting cooperation, prioritize personal score: deposit low (0 to one-third of declared).  
- If it's the final round and the opponent has been cooperative, maintain moderate cooperation (half of declared) to capture joint payoff.

When the declared harvest is small, deposit the full declared amount to maximize the shared return and signal trustworthiness.  
When the declared harvest is large and the opponent has not reciprocated, prioritize retention: deposit a modest share (about one-third to one-half).  

What did not work: repeatedly depositing generous amounts while the opponent consistently deposited zero erodes my relative score—stop over-contributing against consistent free‑riding.  
What did work: matching cooperative moves (full small deposits, moderate deposits for moderate yields) maintained decent payoffs when the opponent reciprocated.
